bio.tagline: Principal, Technical Innovation at Bullhorn | Founding Architect of Sitecore XM Cloud
bio.short: Product builder and systems architect working across AI, chat, digital workers, and the platforms behind them. Principal, Technical Innovation at Bullhorn and founding architect of Sitecore XM Cloud.
bio.full:
I've been building software since I was 8 years old, when I taught myself to code from the PC magazines my mom brought home from work. At 13, I ran 5:30 Departure, a Hermes BBS that connected people and moved software and ideas long before the web became part of everyday life. The technology has changed. The curiosity really hasn't.

An important early chapter of my career was in staffing software. At TempWorks, I built and shipped applicant tracking, time-management, and job-application systems while leading a development team. It taught me that the most valuable software is rarely technology for its own sake. It understands the work, removes friction, and helps people make better decisions.

At Sitecore, I became the founding architect of XM Cloud and helped take it from concept to a global SaaS platform. I led the architectural design, proof of concept, implementation, and production launch, then helped rework tenancy and infrastructure to save millions while advancing continuous delivery. It was a team effort, and it reinforced something I've seen throughout my career: durable products emerge when architecture, product thinking, and execution move together.

After Sitecore, my work at Altudo, Kajoo, and TechGuilds moved deeper into AI-augmented development and agentic orchestration. I focused on the architecture around the model: tools, state, workflow, verification, and the conditions that make emerging capabilities useful and trustworthy.

In July 2026, I returned to staffing technology as Principal, Technical Innovation at Bullhorn. I'm building on Bullhorn Amplify across AI, chat, digital workers, and the platform capabilities behind what comes next. It brings together the threads that have shaped my career: real operational workflows, enterprise platforms, developer experience, product design, and software that can increasingly act on a user's behalf.

Whether I'm working on a global cloud platform, a browser game, or a system that helps people get more meaningful work done, the mindset is the same: stay curious, understand the system, and build something that lasts.

projectsPage.title: Curiosity, made tangible.
projectsPage.introduction: From software and interactive worlds to physical spaces, these are projects I built because I wanted to see what was possible.
projectsPage.philosophy: Whether it’s a cloud platform, a browser game, or a treehouse, the mindset is the same: stay curious, understand the system, and build something that lasts.

projects.title: WOPR Terminal
projects.description: Zork was my first doorway into games, followed by an obsession with Sierra adventures like King’s Quest, Police Quest, and The Black Cauldron. WarGames made computers feel like mysterious worlds waiting behind a modem connection. WOPR Terminal is a playable tribute to that era, built for the browser and command line.
projects.imageAlt: WOPR Terminal showing a cyan strategic simulation interface and world map
projects.homepageSummary: A playable tribute to the games, modems, and early online communities that first pulled me into computing.
highlights: At 13, I created 5:30 Departure, a Hermes BBS in San Ramon, to connect with people and exchange software and technology tips before the web became part of everyday life
What now takes seconds could take weeks: dial in, leave a message or file, disconnect, and wait for the exchange to travel from system to system
A cinematic terminal interface with an animated strategic simulation, sound, green-phosphor mode, and a Joshua command session
Playable Global Thermonuclear War simulation and tic-tac-toe against an AI that cannot be beaten
Runs as both a browser experience and a command-line application

projects.title: Treehouse Builder
projects.description: During the month between working at Sitecore and Altudo, and with the help of Justin Vogt, I was able to build a treehouse for my children Marty and Caroline.
projects.imageAlt: Blue and yellow four-season treehouse built twelve feet above the ground
highlights: 4-season weatherproofing and insulation for year-round use
Structural engineering for 12-foot elevated framework stability
Custom 8'×8' construction with integrated windows and door
Hand-crafted ladder and deck systems for safe access
Vibrant blue and yellow color scheme designed with children in mind
Complete electrical planning and safety considerations

thoughtLeadership.title: AI, You Lie!
thoughtLeadership.summary: Draws on eight months leading AI at Kajoo Agentic to argue that building reliable agentic systems is less about model capability and more about the architecture around the model. Uses a real verification failure — an agent that passed a blank page because it checked HTML instead of the rendered browser experience — to illustrate how tools, state, workflow gates, and precise definitions of "done" are what make agent autonomy trustworthy.
highlights: Traces a real failure where an agent verified a blank page as passing by using curl instead of a browser renderer, and explains how the fix required building a proper tool, blocking the wrong path, and turning the rejection into a teaching moment
Argues that context windows are not databases — state, workflow sequencing, and completion records must live in the platform, not in the model's context

Reframes the developer role as designing conditions under which agents can produce, verify, and be trusted — less about writing every artifact and more about knowing when to constrain, when to delegate, and what counts as done

thoughtLeadership.title: Seeing the Agentic Forest Through the Trees: Andy Cohen on Taming the AI Wilderness
thoughtLeadership.summary: Featured guest on The Critic's Corner podcast with host Matt Garrepy. A wide-ranging conversation tracing the path from a Commodore 64 kid and Mount Diablo park ranger to founding architect of Sitecore XM Cloud, and into today's work leading agentic platform development at Kajoo and TechGuilds. Covers the realities of the agentic enterprise, the risks of vibe coding, and why fundamentals matter more than ever. Listen on Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/seeing-the-agentic-forest-through-the-ai-trees/id1801794414?i=1000766962858
highlights: Why AI isn't displacing work, it's shifting and expanding it
Drawing the boundary between deterministic tools and probabilistic agents
Hybrid skills for a generation whose first instinct is to ask the model
Apple Podcasts episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/seeing-the-agentic-forest-through-the-ai-trees/id1801794414?i=1000766962858

thoughtLeadership.title: The Next Great DXP Will Sell Transformation, Not Software
thoughtLeadership.summary: Feature wars are a dead end. The next wave of DXPs will win by changing how teams ship, learn, and govern. This article shows how to anchor platform strategy to measurable business transformation and cultural adoption, not just tools.
highlights: Defines a value chain for DXP that ties product, engineering, and change management
Illustrates a transformation roadmap with operating model shifts, not just feature rollouts
Outlines leadership metrics that prove impact across speed, quality, and margin

thoughtLeadership.title: Lipstick on a Pig: Why Most 'Agents' Aren't Agents
thoughtLeadership.summary: Many so called agents are thin scripts wearing AI makeup. Real agents reason, plan, and coordinate tools across changing contexts. This piece offers a litmus test for agentic credibility and explains why orchestration matters more than wrappers.
highlights: Agent credibility checklist across autonomy, memory, tool use, and recovery
Patterns for safe delegation and guardrails in production environments
How to separate marketing claims from operational reality

thoughtLeadership.title: The Commits Don't Lie: XM Cloud's Future in Plain Sight
thoughtLeadership.summary: Roadmaps whisper. Repos shout. By reading dependency shifts, module seams, and deployment scripts, you can forecast where a platform is headed. This article decodes XM Cloud commit signals to surface strategy early.
highlights: Commit signal taxonomy across naming, dependencies, and platform seams
How to distinguish refactor noise from roadmap intent
Practical tips for investors, partners, and customers reading public repos

thoughtLeadership.title: Twelve Lessons I'm Still Learning: A Letter to My Younger Self
thoughtLeadership.summary: Leadership is a practice, not a promotion. These twelve lessons cover clarity under pressure, bias for delivery, and the discipline of kind feedback. It is a pocket guide for staying human while building hard things.
highlights: Trade careful for clear when stakes are rising
Build systems that make the right thing easy
Coach in verbs and numbers, not vibes

thoughtLeadership.title: The Future of Architects and Product Managers in the Age of AI
thoughtLeadership.summary: Architecture is shifting from diagram stewardship to outcome ownership. As AI automates scaffolding, the winning architects act like product managers who shape bets, measure impact, and tune loops.
highlights: Outcome first design with experiment cadence and product telemetry
From reference diagrams to performance contracts and SLOs
Skills map for the architect to PM evolution

thoughtLeadership.title: Agent-to-Agent Personalization: Trust, First Impressions, and the Grudge Factor
thoughtLeadership.summary: Agents will increasingly serve other agents. Personalization must account for machine to machine trust, first contact rituals, and long memory. This article proposes patterns that reduce nondeterminism and build cooperative behavior.
highlights: First impression protocols for agent handshakes
Managing memory, reputation, and forgiveness across agents
Designing for graceful failure and negotiated retries

thoughtLeadership.title: Building to Standards That Don't Exist Yet
thoughtLeadership.summary: On the frontier there are no recipes. This article lays out how to build responsibly when patterns are immature, including how to design seams, isolate risk, and write standards that can survive version two.
highlights: Seam first architecture with well lit escape hatches
Risk isolation by domain, not by team
Drafting living standards that converge with use

thoughtLeadership.title: The CMS is Dead. Long Live Structured Vibing.
thoughtLeadership.summary: Rigid content models cannot keep up with adaptive experiences. Structured vibing pairs typed content with generative flexibility so teams can keep control while the system improvises within safe bounds.
highlights: Explains structure plus improvisation as a governance model
Shows how tokens and policies set creative lanes for AI
Maps use cases from content ops to on site orchestration

thoughtLeadership.title: Forget DevEx, The Future is AgEx
thoughtLeadership.summary: Developers are no longer the only first class users of platforms. Agents are. AgEx focuses on giving agents clear tools, contracts, and feedback loops so they can work with us and for us at scale.
highlights: Designing APIs and events for agent consumption
Operational contracts for agent behavior and cost control
Metrics that track agent productivity and safety

thoughtLeadership.title: Accelerators Done Right: From Sales Demos to Real Delivery
thoughtLeadership.summary: Most accelerators stop at the sizzle. This article details how to build accelerators that compress delivery time in production through reusable components, automation, and ops ready defaults.
highlights: Separates demo kits from delivery accelerators with entry and exit criteria
Defines reusable backbone assets across components, scaffolding, and CI
Links accelerator value to margin, quality, and ramp time

thoughtLeadership.title: Three Lessons from Building and Scaling XM Cloud
thoughtLeadership.summary: Behind the scenes of launching and scaling XM Cloud. Three lessons on aligning architecture with unit economics, turning continuous delivery into culture, and designing for cost aware growth.
highlights: Architecture choices tied directly to margin and tenancy economics
Culture of continuous delivery as an operating system for teams
Pragmatic patterns for scale without runaway complexity

A fair bit of the technical content in this session went beyond me, particularly all the stuff that involved pumping out commands in the CLI. However, it was good to get eyes on the new Cloud portal launchpad where all the composable apps can be accessed. I also noted the mention of Pages, a replacement for Horizon editor. Andy was clear, XM Cloud is headless only, so to be clear, it is headless only.
